_meta.indication: BRIVIACT is indicated as adjunctive therapy in the treatment of partial-onset seizures in patients 16 years of age and older with epilepsy.

pivotal_trials.design: Phase 3, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, fixed-dose study conducted in Europe and India, evaluating BRV 20 mg/day, 50 mg/day, and 100 mg/day (4 arms) over a 12-week treatment period
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with partial-onset seizures not adequately controlled with 1 to 2 concomitant AEDs; concomitant levetiracetam limited to <20% of subjects
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Percent reduction in 7-day partial-onset seizure frequency over placebo
pivotal_trials.result: Percent reduction over placebo: 50 mg/day 9.5%, 100 mg/day 17.0%; the primary outcome did not achieve statistical significance under the sequential testing procedure (BRV 100 mg vs placebo only nominally significant)

nct_ctgov.title: Double-blind, Randomized Study Evaluating the Efficacy and Safety of Brivaracetam in Adults With Partial Onset Seizures

pivotal_trials.design: Phase 3, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, fixed-dose global study evaluating BRV 5 mg/day, 20 mg/day, and 50 mg/day (4 arms) over a 12-week treatment period
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with refractory partial-onset seizures on 1 to 2 concomitant AEDs; concomitant levetiracetam limited to 20% of subjects
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Percent reduction in 7-day partial-onset seizure frequency over placebo
pivotal_trials.result: BRV 50 mg/day: 16.9% reduction over placebo, statistically significant (p=0.025)

nct_ctgov.title: Double-blind, Randomized Study Evaluating the Efficacy and Safety of Brivaracetam in Adults With Partial Onset Seizures

pivotal_trials.design: Phase 3, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, fixed-dose global study evaluating BRV 100 mg/day and 200 mg/day (3 arms) over a 12-week treatment period; conducted after N01252 and N01253 with patients on concomitant levetiracetam excluded
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with refractory partial-onset seizures on 1 to 2 concomitant AEDs; patients receiving levetiracetam within 90 days prior to study entry excluded
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Percent reduction in 28-day partial-onset seizure frequency over placebo
pivotal_trials.result: Percent reduction over placebo: 100 mg/day 25.2%, 200 mg/day 25.7%; both doses statistically significant (p<0.001 for both)

nct_ctgov.title: Brivaracetam Efficacy and Safety Study in Subjects With Partial Onset Seizures

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (at least 5% and at least 2% more than placebo) were somnolence and sedation (16% vs 8% placebo), dizziness (12% vs 7%), fatigue (9% vs 4%), and nausea/vomiting (5% vs 3%). Discontinuation due to adverse events was 5%, 8%, and 7% at 50/100/200 mg/day vs 4% for placebo. Labeled warnings include suicidal behavior and ideation, neurological (somnolence/fatigue, dizziness/gait) reactions, psychiatric reactions (13% vs 8% placebo), and hypersensitivity (bronchospasm/angioedema).
target_moa: Brivaracetam displays high and selective affinity for synaptic vesicle protein 2A (SV2A) in the brain; binding to SV2A is considered the primary mechanism for its anticonvulsant activity.

advisory_committee.vote: This application was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because the safety profile is acceptable and the clinical trial design is similar to that of previously approved drugs for the treatment of partial-onset seizures.

description.text: Added use as monotherapy for treatment of partial onset seizures in patients 16 years and older with epilepsy

citations.quote: These Prior Approval supplemental new drug applications provide for the use of BRIVIACT (brivaracetam) as monotherapy for the treatment of partial onset seizures in patients 16 years of age and older with epilepsy.

basis.text: The application was reviewed as a Standard (not Priority) review.

summary.text: BRIVIACT was reviewed and approved as a standard-review NDA under section 505(b) for adjunctive treatment of partial-onset seizures in patients 16 years and older; efficacy was supported by three adequate and well-controlled pivotal Phase 3 trials (N01252, N01253, N01358). It was not referred to an advisory committee, and no accelerated-approval or expedited-program designations were applied. Deferred pediatric studies were required as postmarketing requirements under PREA.

citations.quote: Efficacy is supported by three adequate and well controlled pivotal trials provided in the marketing application (studies 1252, 1253 and 1358).

This application was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because the safety profile is acceptable for the treatment of partial-onset seizures in patients with epilepsy and because the clinical trial design is similar to that of trials of previously approved drugs for the treatment of partial-onset seizures in patients with epilepsy.
Your deferred pediatric studies required under section 505B(a) of the FDCA are required postmarketing studies.

requirement.text: 3042-1: A pharmacokinetic analysis to determine a dosing regimen in children from 4 years to less than 16 years of age that provides drug exposure similar to that effective in adult patients with partial onset seizures.

citations.quote: 3042-1 A pharmacokinetic analysis to determine a dosing regimen in children from 4 years to less than 16 years of age that provides drug exposure that is similar to the exposure that is effective in adult patients with partial onset seizures. This analysis will require pharmacokinetic data from studies of both adult and pediatric patients. These studies have already been performed.

requirement.text: 3042-2: A pharmacokinetic and safety analysis in children from 1 month to less than 16 years of age to determine whether the bioavailability of the intravenous and oral formulations is similar and to determine an acceptable safety margin of the intravenous formulation.

citations.quote: 3042-2 A pharmacokinetic and safety analysis in children from 1 month to less than 16 years of age to determine whether the bioavailability of the intravenous and oral formulations is similar and to determine an acceptable safety margin of the intravenous formulation when administered at doses that are found acceptable for oral administration.

requirement.text: 3042-3: A prospective, randomized, controlled, double-blinded efficacy and safety study of brivaracetam for adjunctive treatment of partial onset seizures in children from 1 month to less than 4 years of age, with primary efficacy endpoint based on video/EEG seizure frequency.

citations.quote: 3042-3 A prospective, randomized, controlled, double-blinded, efficacy and safety study of brivaracetam for the adjunctive treatment of partial onset seizures in children from 1 month to less than 4 years of age. The primary efficacy endpoint during the controlled phase will examine seizure frequency based upon video/electroencephalographic data.

requirement.text: 3042-4: Long-term safety study of brivaracetam in the adjunctive treatment of partial onset seizures in children from 1 month to less than 16 years of age, enrolling at least 200 patients.

citations.quote: 3042-4 Long-term safety study of brivaracetam in the adjunctive treatment of partial onset seizures in children from 1 month to less than 16 years of age. Routine safety measures should be monitored. Behavioral and cognitive endpoints should be included. A total of at least 200 patients must be enrolled. Subjects should be balanced among age cohorts.
